alerts.title: DTG-associated weight gain and metabolic deterioration
alerts.message: Guidelines state weight gain should be discussed when starting all ART, with proactive diet and exercise advice, as obesity is an increasing problem particularly among women. Patient gained 17kg (65→82kg) and BMI rose from 25.6 to 32.4 within 18 months of switching to DTG. Acanthosis nigricans indicates insulin resistance. Fasting glucose worsened from 92 to 118 mg/dL (impaired), HbA1c 6.1% is pre-diabetic. Lipid profile is atherogenic: LDL 148, HDL 38, triglycerides 212 mg/dL. BP rose from 118/74 to 138/88 mmHg. DTG is strongly associated with weight gain; family history of diabetes compounds risk. Non-drug factors like dietary and lifestyle changes may also contribute. Virological suppression is excellent.

evidence.recommended_action: Provide diet and exercise counselling. Monitor fasting glucose and HbA1c every 3 months for first year. Consider weight-loss therapies if available. Evaluate for potential regimen switch if metabolic deterioration continues.

alerts.title: No assessment or plan documented for abnormal labs
alerts.message: Patient has multiple new abnormalities: pre-diabetic HbA1c 6.1%, impaired fasting glucose 118 mg/dL, dyslipidaemia (LDL 148, triglycerides 212 mg/dL), elevated BP 138/88 mmHg, and BMI 32.4. No assessment or plan was documented for this visit. Guidelines recommend glucose monitoring every 3 months for the first year after DTG initiation. These metabolic abnormalities require active clinical management including lifestyle counselling, repeat metabolic monitoring, and potential pharmacologic intervention for dyslipidaemia or hypertension.

evidence.recommended_action: Document assessment and management plan addressing pre-diabetes, dyslipidaemia, hypertension, and obesity. Schedule fasting glucose and HbA1c monitoring every 3 months. Consider lipid-lowering and antihypertensive therapy per guidelines.

alerts.title: Pre-diabetes requires quarterly glucose monitoring on DTG
alerts.message: Guidelines specify glucose monitoring every 3 months for the first year for patients on DTG. Patient has been on DTG for 18 months and now has impaired fasting glucose (118 mg/dL) and pre-diabetic HbA1c (6.1%). No prior glucose monitoring results are recorded since the baseline value of 92 mg/dL at the time of switch. This monitoring gap means the trajectory of glycaemic deterioration is unknown. With family history of type 2 diabetes and acanthosis nigricans, this patient is at high risk of progression to overt diabetes.

evidence.recommended_action: Begin quarterly fasting glucose and HbA1c monitoring. Screen for diabetes with OGCT if indicated. Refer for diabetes prevention programme including diet and exercise intervention.
